build.why: Armor — keeps Nautilus alive through incidental AoE in Steel Path.
Big health pool; sentinels die to stray hits without it.
Shield buffer so it doesn't get one-shot by a stray Bombard rocket.
Precept: restores YOUR shields when they break — free survivability for you.
Faster shield regen keeps both of you topped up.
Precept: heals your Warframe over time — pairs with Guardian for sustain.
Health orbs also repair Nautilus, and boost your armor while it lives.
Enemy + loot radar — QoL that also helps the beam find targets faster.

description: THE meta primer sentinel. Its Verglas Prime cold beam stacks statuses on everything it looks at, and Manifold Bond spreads those statuses around — the setup that feeds Condition Overload and Galvanized mods on your weapons.
farm: Relics (Prime Resurgence rotation) or player trading. The base Nautilus blueprint is in the Market; its parts drop from Corpus missions.
name: Nautilus Prime
notes: Verglas Prime gets its own primer build below. Keep Nautilus on 'follow' in tight tiles so the beam stays on target.

precepts.name: Cordon
precepts.why: Tethers and groups enemies together so the Verglas beam hits the whole pack at once.

precepts.name: Manifold Bond
precepts.why: The engine of the primer: when Nautilus kills, status effects spread to nearby enemies. Farm it from Sisters of Parvos.

build.why: Beam range — the single most important primer stat; longer beam = more primed enemies.
Cold damage; combines with toxin for Viral.
Toxin damage; Cryo + Infected = Viral, the damage-taken debuff your weapons want.
Raw status chance — more procs per second on the beam.
More status chance plus crit damage; beams love both.
Crit chance on the beam; part of the Vigilante set for the set bonus.
Punch-through so the beam primed enemies BEHIND the first target too.
Fire rate = status ticks per second. Faster beam, faster priming.

description: Nautilus Prime's glacial beam. Built for status, not damage: it paints enemies with Viral (and more) so your weapons hit harder via Condition Overload / Galvanized mods.
farm: Comes with Nautilus Prime (relics or trading). No separate farm.
name: Verglas Prime
notes: Do NOT build for damage — a dead enemy can't be primed. Manifold Bond goes on NAUTILUS (the sentinel), not the weapon.

build.why: Armor for Steel Path splash damage.
Health pool — Carrier likes to hover near explosions.
Precept: shield restore for YOU on shield break.
Precept: the whole reason to run Carrier — auto-breaks containers.
Precept: ammo conversion keeps bullet hoses fed.
Precept: heals your Warframe — Carrier becomes a pocket healer.
Radar — spot loot and enemies through walls.

description: The loot vacuum king. Huge pickup radius plus the Looter precept that smashes open every container in range — the lazy farmer's best friend.
farm: Vaulted relics or player trading. The base Carrier blueprint is in the Market; parts drop from Corpus enemies.
name: Carrier Prime
notes: Best general-purpose sentinel for farming, relic runs, and anything where you want loot without thinking.

precepts.name: Looter
precepts.why: Breaks open all loot containers in range — resources, mods, and ayatan stars without you lifting a finger.

precepts.name: Ammo Case
precepts.why: Converts unused ammo pickups into ammo for your current weapon — solves ammo economy.

build.why: Base damage — shotguns scale hard off this.
Toxin + status; pairs with cold for Viral.
Heat + status; enables Blast or Corrosive combos.
Crit chance — set bonus can upgrade YOUR crits.
Fire rate — Carrier fires on its own schedule, so faster is better.

description: Carrier Prime's shotgun. Decent damage with a status build — good enough to strip shields and finish weakened enemies.
farm: Comes with Carrier Prime (vaulted relics or trading).
name: Sweeper Prime
notes: Carrier AI is erratic — don't expect it to focus fire. Build Sweeper for status/AoE value, not precision.

build.why: Armor — Helios likes to float into danger to scan.
Precept: your shields restored on break.
Precept: auto-scan — why you brought Helios.
Precept: heal over time for your Warframe.
Enemies Helios damages drop health orbs on death — sustain engine.

description: The Codex scanner. Investigator auto-scans everything new — finish your Codex and get free Simaris standing without ever pulling out a scanner.
farm: Vaulted relics or player trading. The base Helios is researched in the Tenno Lab of your Clan Dojo.
name: Helios Prime
notes: Bring to any new quest, open world, or Sanctuary Onslaught push — it scans while you fight. Deconstructor Prime hits surprisingly hard with a crit build.

precepts.name: Investigator
precepts.why: Auto-scans unscanned enemies and objects — the entire point of Helios.

precepts.name: Targeting Receptor
precepts.why: Highlights weak points for the Deconstructor to hit.

build.why: Precept: energy orbs from Dethcube kills — feeds energy-hungry frames.
Precept: makes Dethcube actively attack instead of only defending.
Precept: heal sustain on top of damage.

description: The damage sentinel. Vaporize deletes a single target, and the Deth Machine Rifle Prime is one of the hardest-hitting sentinel weapons.
farm: Vaulted relics or player trading. The base Dethcube blueprint is in the Market; parts drop from Infested enemies.
name: Dethcube Prime
notes: Pair with Energy Generator if your frame is energy-hungry — it's a mini Zenurik that also shoots things.

precepts.name: Vaporize
precepts.why: Fires a high-damage beam at one target — deletes Eximus units and heavies.

precepts.name: Energy Generator
precepts.why: Dethcube drops an energy orb on kill with its weapon — energy economy for free.

build.why: Armor — Shade needs to survive to keep cloaking you.
Precept: the invisibility engine — never remove it.
Radar — know when enemies are close enough to trigger Ghost.
Drops rare mods/credits on death — consolation prize if Shade eats a rocket.

description: The stealth sentinel. Ghost turns you invisible whenever enemies get close — a panic button for squishy frames and spy/rescue missions.
farm: Baro Ki'Teer (Void Trader) — appears in his inventory rotation for ducats + credits. The base Shade blueprint is in the Market; parts drop from Corpus enemies.
name: Prisma Shade
notes: Ghost has a cooldown — don't rely on it as permanent stealth. Prisma version has better stats and the shiny Baro look.

precepts.name: Ghost
precepts.why: You go invisible when enemies approach — free stealth for revives, hacks, and escapes.

precepts.name: Revenge
precepts.why: Shade attacks enemies that damage you — deterrent while invisible.

build.why: Precept: close-range zaps for swarm clear.

description: The crowd-control sentinel. Calculated Shot fires arcing electricity that chains between enemies — built-in CC on every shot.
farm: Blueprint in the Market; parts drop from Corpus enemies (notably the Corpus Gas City tileset on Jupiter).
name: Diriga
notes: Underrated pick for defense/mobile defense — the arcs interrupt whole packs. Vulklok can be built for radiation to confuse heavies.

precepts.name: Calculated Shot
precepts.why: Fires electric bolts that arc to nearby enemies — AoE CC on autopilot.

precepts.name: Arc Coil
precepts.why: Tesla-coil zaps around Diriga — point-blank crowd control.

build.why: Armor — stretch the time between Reawakens.
Precept: self-revive — the reason Djinn exists.
Precept: groups enemies for your AoE.
Precept: Djinn revives YOU when you're downed — then Reawaken brings Djinn back. The loop is real.

description: The immortal sentinel. Reawaken revives Djinn itself after death — the only sentinel that refuses to stay dead.
farm: Blueprint in the Market; parts drop from Infested enemies (Deimos / Orokin Derelict missions).
name: Djinn
notes: Sacrifice + Reawaken is the famous combo: Djinn dies reviving you, then revives itself. The most self-sufficient sentinel in the game.

precepts.name: Reawaken
precepts.why: Djinn revives ITSELF 90 seconds after dying — the signature trick no other sentinel has.

precepts.name: Fatal Attraction
precepts.why: Lures enemies toward a gas cloud — soft CC that groups targets.

build.why: Faster shield regen to keep Guardian relevant.

description: The 'get off me' sentinel. Crowd Dispersion knocks back everything that gets close — breathing room for squishy frames.
farm: Vaulted relics or player trading. The base Wyrm blueprint is in the Market.
name: Wyrm Prime
notes: Great pick for frames that hate being touched (Banshee, Nova, casters). Knockback also interrupts Eximus auras briefly.

precepts.name: Crowd Dispersion
precepts.why: Radial knockback when enemies crowd you — instant personal space.

precepts.name: Warrior
precepts.why: Wyrm attacks more aggressively — pairs with the knockback for kiting.

build.why: Consolation loot if the starter bot dies.

description: The starter sentinel — free at the beginning of the game. Molecular Conversion turns damage into overshields, teaching new players the value of shield gating early.
farm: Given free during the tutorial quest; blueprint also in the Market. Artax is its default weapon.
name: Taxon
notes: You'll outgrow Taxon, but Molecular Conversion's overshield trick stays relevant — it's a mini shield-gate engine for free.

precepts.name: Molecular Conversion
precepts.why: Damage Taxon deals converts into overshields for you — free shield gate fuel.

precepts.name: Retarget
precepts.why: Taxon switches to whatever is shooting you — defensive targeting.

build.why: Cold damage — slows enemies hit by the beam.
Toxin; with cold makes Viral for early-game damage scaling.
Beam range — Artax is short-ranged by default.
Fire rate for faster status ticks.
Punch-through to slow packs, not just one enemy.

description: Taxon's cold beam. Applies Cold procs that slow enemies — a baby primer for new players learning status effects.
farm: Comes with Taxon (free starter sentinel); blueprint in the Market.
name: Artax
notes: Think of Artax as training wheels for the Verglas Prime primer concept — same idea, smaller numbers.

build.why: Radar — stacks with the scan precepts for total awareness.
Precept: healing on long mining sessions.

description: The open-world specialist. Scan Matter highlights mining/fishing spots and Scan Aquatic Lifeforms marks fish — mandatory gear for Fortuna/Plains/Deimos resource runs.
farm: Researched in the Tenno Lab of your Clan Dojo (blueprint + parts from Dojo research).
name: Oxylus
notes: Swap to Oxylus before any dedicated mining/fishing run — the highlight precepts save enormous time. Multron is a serviceable burst weapon.

precepts.name: Scan Matter
precepts.why: Highlights mining nodes and plants — never miss a gem vein again.

precepts.name: Scan Aquatic Lifeforms
precepts.why: Highlights fish in water — speeds up fishing massively.

description: The base stealth sentinel — Ghost invisibility on demand. Prisma Shade (Baro) is the direct upgrade.
farm: Blueprint in the Market; parts drop from Corpus enemies.
name: Shade
notes: Strictly worse than Prisma Shade — upgrade when Baro brings it. Fine as a placeholder for spy/sabotage missions.

precepts.name: Ghost
precepts.why: Invisibility when enemies approach — the stealth panic button.

precepts.name: Revenge
precepts.why: Retaliates against attackers.

description: Base version of the damage sentinel. Same Vaporize/Energy Generator kit as the Prime, lower stats.
farm: Blueprint in the Market; parts drop from Infested enemies.
name: Dethcube
notes: A solid placeholder until you get Dethcube Prime from trading or unvaulting.

precepts.name: Vaporize
precepts.why: High-damage beam nuke on one target.

precepts.name: Energy Generator
precepts.why: Energy orbs from Dethcube kills.

description: Base scanner sentinel from Clan Dojo research. Same Investigator kit as Helios Prime.
farm: Researched in the Tenno Lab of your Clan Dojo.
name: Helios
notes: Upgrade to Helios Prime when you can — same job, better stats and Deconstructor Prime.

precepts.name: Investigator
precepts.why: Auto-scan — the Codex completer.

precepts.name: Targeting Receptor
precepts.why: Weak-point targeting.

description: Base primer sentinel. Cordon groups enemies; the Prime's Verglas is the upgrade that makes the meta build sing.
farm: Blueprint in the Market; parts drop from Corpus missions.
name: Nautilus
notes: Works as a budget primer with a status Cordon build, but Nautilus Prime + Verglas Prime is the real meta — upgrade when you can.

precepts.name: Cordon
precepts.why: Tethers and groups enemies for AoE.

precepts.name: Manifold Bond
precepts.why: Status spread on kill — farm from Sisters of Parvos.

build.why: Extends Charm buff duration — longer double-loot windows.
Scales off YOUR max health — big EHP for the cat.
Scales off your armor — makes the cat tanky.
Scales off your shields — completes the Link trio.
Your melee kills heal Smeeta — keeps it alive in Steel Path.
Loot + enemy radar — you want to SEE the loot Charm doubles.
Beast vacuum — pulls loot to you so nothing gets missed.

description: THE loot pet. Charm randomly grants buffs including a 2-minute double-affinity/double-resource window — nothing else in the game doubles your loot like this.
farm: Scan Feral Kavats on Deimos (Cambion Drift) with a Codex/ Synthesis Scanner until you have 10 Kavat Genetic Codes, then incubate in the Incubator (needs the Kavat Incubator Segment from the Dojo or Market). Breeding is random between Smeeta/Adarza/Vasca — use imprints to force Smeeta.
name: Smeeta Kavat
notes: Bring Smeeta to EVERY farm: relics, resources, affinity, Steel Path. The Charm double-dip also applies to pickups like Argon Crystals and open-world gems.

precepts.name: Charm
precepts.why: Random buffs every ~27s — the jackpot is 120s of double affinity AND double resource drops. The most valuable buff in the game.

precepts.name: Mischief
precepts.why: Decoy that draws fire — keeps the squishy cat alive.

build.why: Precept: the crit buff — why Adarza exists.
Adarza's attacks strip armor — armor strip on a pet is premium.

description: The crit pet. Cat's Eye gives +60% crit chance to the whole squad periodically — massive for crit weapons and Eidolon hunts.
farm: Same as Smeeta: 10 Kavat Genetic Codes from scanning Feral Kavats on Deimos, then incubate. Random breed — use Adarza imprints to guarantee it.
name: Adarza Kavat
notes: The Eidolon-hunt pick before you have a full squad buffer setup — Cat's Eye timing with your amp shots matters. Also great for crit-melee builds.

precepts.name: Cat's Eye
precepts.why: +60% critical chance for 10s to the squad — turns good crit weapons into red-crit monsters.

precepts.name: Reflect
precepts.why: Reflects damage back at attackers — defensive filler.

build.why: Precept: revive utility — clutch in Steel Path.
Crit damage for the cat's own attacks.

description: The vampire pet. Drain latches onto enemies and siphons health to you — sustain for frames without healing.
farm: Same as Smeeta/Adarza: 10 Kavat Genetic Codes from Feral Kavats on Deimos, incubate. Use Vasca imprints to force the breed.
name: Vasca Kavat
notes: Niche but beloved — the Transfusion revive has saved more Steel Path runs than people admit. Less loot value than Smeeta, more sustain.

precepts.name: Drain
precepts.why: Latches onto an enemy and drains health to heal you — lifesteal on demand.

precepts.name: Transfusion
precepts.why: Revives a downed ally (or you) — the cat plays medic.

build.why: Your melee kills heal the dog.
Crit damage — Kubrows hit hard with crit.

description: The stealth dog. Stalk cloaks you when you stand still — classic pick for spy, rescue, and riven challenges.
farm: Buy the Huras Kubrow imprint blueprint from Maroo's Bazaar (Maroo, Earth). Then get a Kubrow Egg from Kubrow dens on Earth (E Prime exterminate is the classic farm), and incubate in the Incubator. Random breed — use two Huras imprints to guarantee it. NOTE: Kubrows have no Prime variants.
name: Huras Kubrow
notes: Remember to manage loyalty/stasis — Kubrows need gene-masks/DNA stabilizers or they lose health. Kavats and sentinels don't have this upkeep, which is why many players prefer them.

precepts.name: Stalk
precepts.why: Cloaks you after standing still a few seconds — free stealth for hacks and revives.

precepts.name: Hunt
precepts.why: Charges and knocks down an enemy — CC on demand.

description: The bodyguard dog. Protect restores your shields and Howl fears enemies — defensive utility for squishy frames.
farm: Raksa imprint blueprint from Maroo's Bazaar + Kubrow Egg from Earth dens, then incubate. Use Raksa imprints to guarantee the breed. No Prime variants exist for Kubrows.
name: Raksa Kubrow
notes: Good training-wheels companion for new players on fragile frames like Banshee or Mirage.

precepts.name: Protect
precepts.why: Restores your shields when they break — a second Guardian.

precepts.name: Howl
precepts.why: Fears nearby enemies — breathing room on demand.

build.why: Vacuum to grab what Dig unearths.

description: The digger dog. Dig unearths energy orbs, ammo, and credits — the Kubrow answer to energy economy.
farm: Sahasa imprint blueprint from Maroo's Bazaar + Kubrow Egg from Earth dens, then incubate. Use Sahasa imprints to guarantee it. No Prime variants exist for Kubrows.
name: Sahasa Kubrow
notes: Outclassed by Smeeta for loot and Zenurik for energy, but Sahasa does both at once with zero effort — a fine all-rounder.

precepts.name: Dig
precepts.why: Digs up energy orbs, ammo, and credits periodically — free economy.

precepts.name: Ferocity
precepts.why: Bonus damage against knocked-down enemies — pairs with Hunt.

description: The hunter dog. Unleash deals heavy finisher damage to a target — deletes priority enemies on command.
farm: Sunika imprint blueprint from Maroo's Bazaar + Kubrow Egg from Earth dens, then incubate. Use Sunika imprints to guarantee it. No Prime variants exist for Kubrows.
name: Sunika Kubrow
notes: Niche pick for assassination-style play. The finisher damage scales well into Steel Path against single targets.

precepts.name: Unleash
precepts.why: Massive finisher damage to a single target — assassinates heavies and Eximus.

precepts.name: Savagery
precepts.why: Bonus finisher damage — stacks with Unleash.

build.why: Vacuum — stacks with Retrieve for total pickup coverage.

description: The retriever dog. Retrieve picks up ammo, energy, and mods for you — a vacuum with legs.
farm: Chesa imprint blueprint from Maroo's Bazaar + Kubrow Egg from Earth dens, then incubate. Use Chesa imprints to guarantee it. No Prime variants exist for Kubrows.
name: Chesa Kubrow
notes: Largely replaced by the Fetch mod + Carrier, but Chesa + Fetch together is maximum laziness for loot.

precepts.name: Retrieve
precepts.why: Fetches pickups (ammo, energy, credits) and brings them to you.

precepts.name: Neutralize
precepts.why: Disarms enemies — bonus utility.

build.why: MOAs use sentinel defensive mods too — shield buffer.

description: The tank MOA model from Fortuna. Built at Legs — pick the model for the look and base stats, then customize with parts.
farm: Buy the Oloro model blueprint from Legs in Fortuna (Solaris United standing). MOA parts (bracket, core, gyro) are crafted from resources or bought from Legs. Assemble in the Foundry.
name: Oloro MOA
notes: Oloro is the tankiest model — best base for Steel Path MOA builds. MOAs use both beast Link mods and sentinel defensive mods.

precepts.name: Stasis Field
precepts.why: Slows projectiles in a bubble — team survivability.

precepts.name: Whiplash Mine
precepts.why: Knockdown mine for area denial.

build.why: Aggressive targeting for a damage MOA.

description: The attack MOA model from Fortuna. Highest damage orientation of the three models.
farm: Buy the Draugen model blueprint from Legs in Fortuna (Solaris United standing); parts crafted or bought from Legs. Assemble in the Foundry.
name: Draugen MOA
notes: Pair Draugen with a hard-hitting MOA weapon (e.g., a cryo/rad build) and it becomes a legitimate DPS companion.

precepts.name: Whiplash Mine
precepts.why: Knockdown mine — area denial while it shoots.

precepts.name: Anti-Grav Grenade
precepts.why: Lifts enemies into the air — sets up headshots and suspends attackers.

build.why: Precept: auto-hack — unique utility no other companion has.

description: The support MOA model from Fortuna. Balanced stats with a utility lean — the flexible middle ground.
farm: Buy the Para model blueprint from Legs in Fortuna (Solaris United standing); parts crafted or bought from Legs. Assemble in the Foundry.
name: Para MOA
notes: Security Override is Para's party trick — it hacks spy vault consoles and even Bursas. Great QoL for Corpus tilesets.

precepts.name: Stasis Field
precepts.why: Slows incoming projectiles — defensive support.

precepts.name: Security Override
precepts.why: Hacks nearby consoles andbursas — free objective progress.

build.why: Precept: deletes Nullifier bubbles — irreplaceable utility.
Precept: status spread — keep if running a primer Hound, swap for damage otherwise.

description: Robotic dogs built from Sister Hound parts. Three models — Bhaira (damage), Urga (utility), Heka (tank) — and the source of the famous Manifold Bond primer mod.
farm: Hunt Sisters of Parvos (spawn a Sister with a Zenith Granum Crown, then defeat her). Hound parts (chassis, etc.) drop from Sisters; combine the parts in the Foundry. Different parts give different models: Bhaira = damage, Urga = utility, Heka = tank.
name: Hound (Sisters of Parvos)
notes: Even if you run Nautilus as your primer, farm a Hound once — Null Audit alone is worth it, and Manifold Bond is the mod that makes the meta work.

precepts.name: Manifold Bond
precepts.why: Status spread on kill — the primer engine. ALSO works on Nautilus, which is the meta combo.

precepts.name: Repo Audit
precepts.why: Disarms enemies — strips guns from Corpus/Grineer.

precepts.name: Null Audit
precepts.why: Pops Nullifier bubbles — the bane of every mission, solved by your dog.

precepts.name: Synergized Prospectus
precepts.why: Loot radar + highlights rare containers.

build.why: Precept: the self-revive — the entire reason Vulpaphylas are meta.
EHP scaling — more health = longer before devolution triggers.
Your melee kills heal it back to full.
The pet's crits heal YOU — sustain loop.
Vacuum — loot collection on an unkillable pet.

description: THE meta pet. When a Vulpaphyla dies it collapses into an invulnerable larval form and revives itself — effectively immortal. Sly's stealth kit makes it the Steel Path survival pick.
farm: Capture (weaken, don't kill) a wild Sly Vulpaphyla in the Cambion Drift on Deimos with a Tranq Rifle, then take it to Son in the Necralisk to incubate. Son also sells the mutagen/antigen combos if you want to re-breed traits.
name: Sly Vulpaphyla
notes: The Steel Path default: it literally cannot stay dead. Sly's invisibility means it rarely even needs the revive.

precepts.name: Crescent Devolution
precepts.why: On death becomes an invulnerable larva, then revives — the immortality mechanic.

precepts.name: Sly Devolution
precepts.why: Sly's stealth: goes invisible, drawing less aggro while it revives.

precepts.name: Survival Instincts
precepts.why: Boosts the larva's survival — faster, safer revives.

build.why: Precept: the Viral primer — why Panzer competes with Sly.

description: The viral pet. Viral Quills sprays Viral procs on everything nearby — a walking primer that also can't die (larva revive).
farm: Tranquilize a wild Panzer Vulpaphyla in the Cambion Drift on Deimos, then incubate with Son in the Necralisk.
name: Panzer Vulpaphyla
notes: Pick Panzer if your weapons need Viral help, Sly if you need pure survival. Both share the immortal larva mechanic.

precepts.name: Viral Quills
precepts.why: Fires quills that apply Viral — free damage-taken debuff on everything around you.

precepts.name: Crescent Devolution
precepts.why: Invulnerable larva self-revive on death.

precepts.name: Panzer Devolution
precepts.why: Explodes into Viral on devolving — death itself becomes a primer.

description: The support Vulpaphyla. Crescent Charge buffs allies — the team-player variant of the immortal pet family.
farm: Tranquilize a wild Crescent Vulpaphyla in the Cambion Drift on Deimos, then incubate with Son in the Necralisk.
name: Crescent Vulpaphyla
notes: The least-picked Vulpaphyla, but the buff is real in coordinated squads — and it still can't die.

precepts.name: Crescent Charge
precepts.why: Charges enemies and buffs nearby allies — support on legs.

precepts.name: Crescent Devolution
precepts.why: Invulnerable larva self-revive on death.

description: The stealth Predasite from Deimos. Ipecac spits corrosive projectiles — armor-eating spit on an immortal-ish frame.
farm: Tranquilize a wild Medjay Predasite in the Cambion Drift on Deimos, then incubate with Son in the Necralisk. Predasites use the same Son system as Vulpaphylas.
name: Medjay Predasite
notes: Predasites don't get the Vulpaphyla larva revive, so they're squishier — Medjay's stealth devolution compensates.

precepts.name: Ipecac
precepts.why: Spits corrosive bile — Corrosive procs strip armor.

precepts.name: Medjay Devolution
precepts.why: Stealth on heavy damage — slips away instead of dying.

build.why: Pet crits heal you — sustain loop.

description: The tank Predasite from Deimos. Anabolic Pollination spreads healing spores — sustain for the squad.
farm: Tranquilize a wild Pharaoh Predasite in the Cambion Drift on Deimos, then incubate with Son in the Necralisk.
name: Pharaoh Predasite
notes: The healer Predasite — pairs well with frames that lack sustain but don't want to run Smeeta.

precepts.name: Anabolic Pollination
precepts.why: Releases healing spores — AoE sustain around the pet.

precepts.name: Pharaoh Devolution
precepts.why: Damage reduction when hurt — tank devolution.

description: The support Predasite from Deimos. Paralytic Spores CC enemies — crowd control on a leash.
farm: Tranquilize a wild Vizier Predasite in the Cambion Drift on Deimos, then incubate with Son in the Necralisk.
name: Vizier Predasite
notes: Niche CC pet — fun in defense missions where the spore field covers a lane.

precepts.name: Paralytic Spores
precepts.why: Spore clouds that slow/stun enemies — soft CC field.

precepts.name: Vizier Devolution
precepts.why: Evasive devolution when heavily damaged.
